column5: Stale line pin in an old oracle after the change shifted a line; ticket does not reach it.
Brief builder cuts the ticket at generated-section heading names; any reading requires not truncating requirements.
Ticket never says what the probe does when bwrap is in a user-writable directory; several reasonable handlings exist.
Pre-existing pane-state reading wrongly passes a live launch as settled; any reading of the ticket requires not closing live work.
Text is only the coachman's disposition fragment, not the finding; too short to tell.
Text is only a disposition fragment; it does not state what the finding claims.
Text is only a dismissal fragment; the finding itself is not stated.
Text is only a disposition fragment referring to another finding; the claim is not stated.
Text is only a disposition about a control test; the finding's claim is not stated.
Text is only a dismissal fragment; the finding itself is not stated.
Missing guard for external targets without an index or checker; one sane answer, no fixture run for them.
Ambiguous detector name and a path without a directory (exit 128); wording defects with one sane fix.
Ticket never says which copy of the checker a re-check runs; finding reverses the fix's scored-copy choice.
Criterion 1 says each file is covered whole; leaving the entrypoint outside the region contradicts it.
Criterion 1 and the direction cover whole files; unmapped sentences in a listed file contradict the ticket.
Ticket never says how a repeat runs when BASE lacks the checker, as on an introduction branch.
A failed git read treated as absent fails open; any reading requires erroring, not reporting no change.
Dispatch input interpolated into a run script is an injection hole; any reading requires binding it safely.
Criteria 1, 13, 14 and D8 require a recorded wall that gates progress; a lost record violates them.
Parsing flaw on paths with spaces and ticket-section lines; ticket states nothing, any reading requires correct parsing.
D5 says unrecognised reset shapes yield no time, because a wrong time is worse than none.
Unreadable log must not read as no walls; criteria 13 and 14 require gating, so failing open is wrong.
Text holds only a target and a severity; no claim is stated.
The code's own message says on or off; accepting a typo contradicts it, so one sane fix.
Existing stdin handling of the dash argument regressed; ticket does not reach it, any reading requires preserving it.
A subdirectory target misses the repository-root settings; criterion 2 requires them read, one sane answer.
Criterion 2 and C2 require project limits for the postmaster launch; the argument placement is a plain defect.
Ticket never says what a relative env_file in project settings is relative to; several reasonable bases.
Criterion 3 requires settings that are complete; a file with only legacy facts is not, so one sane answer.
Ticket says complete project settings need no global config, not what happens when that path exists but is unreadable.
The same setting resolves differently for project and run launches; one sane answer is a shared base.
Criterion 4 requires tracked settings used only once accepted; failing open when git refuses the repository violates it.
Locating the waybill's generated Team section is an input-shape bug; any reading requires ignoring a ticket's own heading.
Criteria 4 and 7 require aftercare after a merge and recognising a merged pull request; re-landing is a defect.
Criterion 2 says the card carries the gates' results; a check letting passing results be omitted contradicts it.
Runbook writes omit the actor argument the script requires; a plain interface mismatch with one fix.
The dispatcher must tell two states apart after a crash; one sane answer, nothing to choose.
A crash before marker removal must not redo landing; the one sane answer is an idempotent resume.
Criterion 7 states head-is-not-BASE and an empty-branch control; skipping on an empty diff contradicts it.
Ticket never says which checks must pass for landing, or what a not-run journey means for journey-less tickets.
Criterion 7 names the provider-reported squash merge as landed; an AND that stalls it contradicts the ticket.
Criterion 7 requires card results to match verify.sh results; written and checked shapes differing breaks that.
Labels must use the checkpoint's own vocabulary; outside the criteria, one sane answer.
Criterion 7 lists an empty branch after the default moves as a control shape; skipping on it is wrong.
A check with no logged result cannot be a pass; criterion 7 names the shape, one sane answer.
Conflated terms are a wording defect with one sane fix; the ticket does not reach finding states.
A landing script must not deadlock on a pruned branch; any reading requires handling an unresolvable head.
A re-verify loop is a defect; any reading requires a way out when the reported head differs.
Criterion 7 and D20 dispatch when there is room; emitting every ready ticket past max_runs contradicts that.
Ticket never says how readiness works for other-kind trackers beyond labels; several reasonable paths exist.
The runbook's logging step and the project logger disagree on a shape; ticket does not reach it.
trackers.md already requires every tracker write be logged; the code logs only one write, so it is wrong.
Clamping a cited range past end of file and reporting same is a wrong comparison under D16.
Two projects' clerks must coexist; a name collision is a defect with one sane fix, not a choice.
C14 and C18 do not fail a premise-stop run with no dispatch; the check contradicts them.
D2 needs a real ready mark; one label containing a comma must not count as ready.
Criterion 7 requires dispatch with no further word; a runbook path that never starts the watcher contradicts it.
D4 requires the mark taken off when a clerk opens; a failed read must not skip that.
Ticket never says what happens to sign-off when the ticket is edited afterwards; binding, ignoring or unmarking all reasonable.
A malformed marker must not read as none; failing open defeats the sign-off binding, one sane answer.
Ticket never says how a premise send-back works on trackers with no adapter or labels; several reasonable paths.
A comment after sign-off must not count as a change; one sane answer, no ticket choice.
Mark's edit base and the adapter's comparison disagree; a plain defect with no choice to make.
Digesting the stored body is the only sound answer; a heuristic cut binds weakly.
Same comma-splitting label defect as the round-3 finding, at another flag; one sane answer.
Queue and check digest different texts, so a commented ticket falsely refuses; a plain mismatch.
Ticket never says how sign-off treats an edit racing the mark; verify-and-roll-back is one of several answers.
